sources.title: Why Information Security is Hard—An Economic Perspective
sources.publicationVersionDate: ACSAC 2001 primary conference paper; PDF metadata created 2001-10-02, modified 2001-10-11
sources.sourceType: Primary conference paper hosted by the conference
sources.actualReading: Complete 8-page PDF extracted and read; title/abstract, §§1–2, liability and offense/defense discussions, conclusion and references checked.
sources.locators: PDF pp. 1–8; printed paper pages 358–365 per conference proceedings citation. Claims used from abstract and §§1–2, conclusion.
sources.supports: Security incentives, externalities, assignment of responsibility/liability, and the possibility that protector and loss bearer differ; no crypto incident rate.
sources.limits: Conceptual argument and cases from the security context of its publication; no cryptocurrency exposure or outcome estimate.

sources.title: Bank Runs, Deposit Insurance, and Liquidity

sources.sourceType: Primary journal article scan hosted by an economics department
sources.actualReading: Abstract, introduction and selected model/contract passages read; full PDF retained.

sources.title: Financial Contagion

sources.actualReading: Primary body abstract, introduction and model setup inspected from retained local PDF text.

sources.title: Communication Theory of Secrecy Systems

sources.sourceType: Primary journal PDF read in browser-rendered form; not locally captured
sources.actualReading: Rendered complete PDF opened; §10 perfect-secrecy discussion/Theorem 6 and key-count example read. Local curl of the source PDF returned HTTP 403; Wiley page provided citation metadata, not article body.
sources.locators: Printed §10, pp. 679–683; Theorem 6 at printed pp. 680–681; key-count argument/example pp. 681–682. Browser-rendered PDF parser locators in session correspond to body lines 3038–3109.

sources.limits: Narrow secrecy model only; no authentication, implementation leakage or deployment claim. No original body byte hash; `sources/SHANNON-READING-RECEIPT.md` hash belongs to the receipt only.

sources.title: CryptanalysisBench: Can LLMs do Cryptanalysis?
sources.authors: Lukas Fluri; Avital Shafran; Nicholas Carlini; Matthew Jagielski; Milad Nasr; Orr Dunkelman; Eyal Ronen; Florian Tramèr
sources.actualReading: PDF abstract/introduction, §4.2 full-strength results, printed p. 9, and conclusion, p. 17 read.
sources.locators: Abstract/PDF pp. 1–2; §4.2 and full-strength breaks, printed p. 9; conclusion, printed p. 17.
sources.supports: Authors report 191 tasks; across evaluated models 14 distinct full-strength scheme breaks, only two author-classified as design flaws; remaining categories include implementation and specification issues. Preprint makes benchmark/taxonomy-specific claims.
sources.limits: No transfer to deployed Bitcoin/Ethereum, no population attack rate, no deployment probability; no code or attack run in this work.

sources.locators: Theorem 6.1, PDF pp. 10–11; §6.1 cost estimates, pp. 11–12; §6.2 two HAWK-256 author-run recoveries/sign-verify, pp. 12–13; Appendix A code description, p. 19.
